officer.body:
Hi Kit,

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are a few thoughts on the outturn report that went to Cabinet on 8 June and Full Council on 15 July. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it.

A cross-check first, and it came out well. We hold 21 PWLB loans for Hastings totalling £63,397,500, which is the same £63,397,500 that closes your Table 5 at 31 March 2026. Our weighted average is 2.82% against your printed 2.81%, and the same total closes Table 1 of the strategy paper as well. So we're certainly looking at the same book.

The thing that struck us is the shape. Of those 21 loans, 13 sit in the 25-years-and-over bucket — £47.2m of principal at an average 2.49%. Only £3m matures in 2028 (the £1m at 2.42% in June and the £2m at 1.98% in December). The single loan above par on the DMO's premature repayment curve today is the £7.5m at 4.80% running to February 2033; the other nineteen live loans are all below. That is a book we couldn't build now, and it is the mirror image of most of what we've read this year — where the near-term maturity bucket is typically the biggest concern.

Paragraph 48 concludes rescheduling was 'unviable' at the roughly 1% differential your advisers saw through 2025/26. On the DMO's published premature-repayment curve today — notice 314/26 PM, 14 August — the direction is still discount rather than premium: across the 20 live loans, an indicative net discount of around £17.8m against £62.2m of principal outstanding. That's not a recommendation and it isn't a quote; only the DMO can quote, it models no MRP or accounting treatment, and whether anything is worth doing turns on replacement cost we don't model. It's just the picture our engine draws, and it will look different by the time your next quarterly report is written. Your book priced daily is at pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis.

One number from Table 4 (page 11) is worth flagging separately — the £5m at 6.00% lent to LB Bexley from 3 November to 7 April. Six per cent for five-month LA money is materially above the distribution we've been seeing this year of the councils we've read. Inter-authority lending is the market nobody publishes, so what other authorities are actually paying for one, three and six-month money can be hard to see. We track it across the sector; the picture is at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity, and July's monthly PWLB total was £368m across 33 loans from 19 borrowers at an average 5.02%, after the thinnest May in years.

None of it needs a meeting or a subscription, and the rates page at pwlbtoday.org/dashboard takes ten seconds to check. On training, four fit Hastings. PWLB break costs — mechanics & live calculator is where the paragraph 48 conversation actually happens on today's curve. Intra-LA borrowing & lending markets is the one for the Bexley trade and the deposit book. Money Market Funds (CNAV / LVNAV / VNAV) picks up the strategy the report says is now the mainstay for surplus cash. And our liability benchmark pathway is interactive and built on live data — worth a look given where CIPFA is heading with the Prudential and Treasury Codes. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts for the whole team.

And if you do find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.
